[BugFix][Sampler] Fix inf in Qwen30b RL sampling by recording stream for q (#13394)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR fixes an `inf` sampling issue observed in Qwen3 30B RL workloads
on Ascend.

In `random_sample()`, tensor `q` is allocated on `global_stream()` but
consumed on `torch.npu.current_stream()` via `probs.div_(q)`. The code
only establishes an execution dependency (`wait_stream`), but does not
declare the storage lifetime of `q` on the consumer stream.

Without `q.record_stream(torch.npu.current_stream())`, the caching
allocator may reclaim and reuse `q`'s buffer on the sampling stream
before the queued division on the current stream has read it. On Ascend,
`exponential_()` is a multi-kernel in-place sequence (`uniform_ -> neg_
-> add_(1) -> masked_fill_ -> log_ -> mul_(-1)`), so the next decode
step's negative intermediate state can overwrite the old `q` address
while the previous consumer is still reading it.

For Qwen3 30B RL (vocab size 151936 vs. tokenizer length 151669), the
masked tail of 267 ids has exactly zero probability. With a corrupted
`q`, `0 / negative_q = -0` wins `argmax` and selects the first masked
OOV id (`151669`), whose raw logprob is `-inf`. The OOV token then
enters the autoregressive context and corrupts all subsequent outputs.

Adding `q.record_stream(torch.npu.current_stream())` declares that `q`
must remain alive on the consumer stream, preventing the allocator from
recycling the buffer too early.

Reproduction with the real `exponential_()` intermediate-state race:
- Before fix: 64/64 rows selected the masked OOV id `151669` with raw
logprob `-inf`
- After fix: 0/64 rows invalid, sampled ids stay legal

Note: the same fix is being submitted against all supported release
branches (`releases/v0.13.0` -> `main`).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

- Reproduced the allocator-reuse race with real `exponential_()`
intermediate states (`uniform_ -> neg_`): 64/64 sampled rows selected
the masked OOV id `151669` with raw logprob `-inf` before the fix; after
the fix 0/64 rows are invalid and sampled ids stay legal.
- Verified natural address reuse of `q` across consecutive decode steps
is eliminated with `record_stream`.
- Existing sampler unit tests pass.
- NPU hardware verification pending on the original RL environment
(`bsz=256, decode>=10k, TP=4, n=8`).

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/d02df748bf9efd99022f1a062597dc3cb3808485

[Feature][EPLB] Integrate upstream EPLB with Model Runner V2 (#12804)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR integrates upstream vLLM EPLB with the Ascend Model Runner V2
path. The architecture decision is tracked in [RFC
#13410](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/13410); the
current runtime model and invariants are documented in the [Model Runner
V2 EPLB
Architecture](https://github.com/freyfwt/vllm-ascend/blob/model-runner-v2-eplb/docs/source/developer_guide/Design_Documents/model_runner_v2_eplb.md).

- Reuses upstream `EPLBController`, `EplbState`, load windows, policy,
placement, and rearrangement lifecycle. Ascend subclasses own batch load
filtering and the device lookup derived from committed placement.
- Keeps the platform patch at capability and construction boundaries.
`HcclEplbCommunicator` reuses the upstream torch-distributed transfer
protocol while expressing the HCCL profiling-buffer capability.
- Moves Model Runner V2 expert routing into `AscendRoutedExperts`: the
upstream router selects logical experts once, an instance adapter maps
them through the upstream `hash_indices_table`, and quantized fused MoE
consumes physical IDs. Executed physical-expert load is recorded after
compute.
- Adds quantization-owned weight views for the tensors actually consumed
by compute. BF16/FP16, W8A8, W4A8, W4A4 MXFP, and W8A8 MXFP have defined
paths; W4A16, W4A16 MXFP, and W4A8 MXFP fail startup validation.
- Adds `additional_config.eplb_config.load_scope=all|prefill|decode`,
preserves the legacy Model Runner V1 EPLB path, and rejects mixed V1/V2
configuration.
- Preserves DeepSeek V4 hash routing while separating routed compute
from quantization methods.

The current scope is synchronous EPLB in the validated standard eager
path. Asynchronous EPLB is rejected at startup. Review hotspots are
placement-to-lookup commit ordering, quantization weight-view
correctness, and the single-routing invariant.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Model Runner V2 users can enable upstream synchronous EPLB with
`--enable-eplb --eplb-config.use_async false` on supported MoE layouts.
`load_scope` selects whether all, prefill, or decode batches contribute
to the load window. Unsupported layouts and conflicting legacy controls
now fail during initialization. See the [EPLB user
guide](https://github.com/freyfwt/vllm-ascend/blob/model-runner-v2-eplb/docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/expert_parallelism_load_balancer.md)
for the support matrix and configuration.

workflow, shell, import, package-layout, and symbolic-shape hooks
passed. The offline gitleaks hook could not run because its downloader

[BugFix][MoE] Fix W8A8 scale handling for dynamic EPLB (#13414)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR fixes W8A8 MoE scale handling for the `swigluoai_uninterleave`
path when dynamic EPLB provides list-form local physical expert weights
and scales.

With dynamic EPLB enabled, a MoE layer may receive one weight tensor and
one scale tensor per local physical expert. However, some MoE MLP paths
previously passed all local expert weights while only using the first
`w1_scale`. This made the weight and scale inputs inconsistent and could
cause NPU operator shape errors.

This PR updates the scale preparation logic for the
`swigluoai_uninterleave` path to:

* pass all local physical expert scales to grouped matmul in the

[BugFix][P/D] Lower Mooncake KV metadata mismatch log level (#13542)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Changes the Mooncake remote/local kv_group2layeridx difference message
from warning to debug and asks users to inspect the printed metadata in
the context of their configured parallelism and KV cache layouts.

kv_group2layeridx describes a worker-local KV cache layout rather than a
canonical global protocol that must be byte-for-byte identical on both
sides. Full dictionaries can therefore differ during valid deployments.
Common examples include:

- Heterogeneous P/D tensor parallelism, where TP-local cache shapes,
block sizes, and padded page sizes differ according to the TP ratio.
- Prefill pipeline parallelism with Decode PP1, where each remote P
stage advertises only the layers owned by that stage while the local D
worker owns the complete layer set.
- Other model, cache, or execution settings that change per-worker
CacheSpec fields, cache-group composition, or layer ownership.

Not every parallelism difference necessarily changes kv_group2layeridx,
and a difference can also expose a real configuration incompatibility.
Full-dictionary inequality alone is therefore not sufficient to emit a
warning. The complete remote and local metadata remain available at
debug level so users can determine whether a particular difference is
expected.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes. Remote/local metadata differences no longer appear in warning-level
logs. The debug message uses neutral wording and directs users to
evaluate the printed metadata against their actual parallel and KV cache
configuration.

[BugFix][Core][Scheduler] Sync recompute cache handling (#13503)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`RecomputeScheduler` copies the upstream scheduling loop so that
decode-side allocation pressure can trigger the PD recompute flow. The
main branch already carries the current Mamba split and
transfer-parameter contracts, but its copied loop is still missing two
upstream hybrid-cache behaviors:

- blocks populated by an asynchronous KV load must be excluded from
same-step zeroing, and unwritten blocks must be re-recorded for zeroing
after a failed load;
- hybrid partial-prefix copy-on-write operations must be forwarded in
`SchedulerOutput`, with their endpoint blocks retained until the
execution fence completes.

Without the first behavior, zeroing may race an out-of-band KV/KDA load.
Without the second, a partial hybrid-cache hit may observe an uncopied
or prematurely reused tail block.

This main-branch fix is intended to land before the corresponding v0.26
backport in #13408.

No open main-branch PR was found covering these `RecomputeScheduler`
gaps.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Recompute scheduling preserves asynchronously loaded state and
hybrid partial-prefix cache copies consistently with the upstream
scheduler.

[Performance][KV Pool] Use Yuanrong multi-buffer APIs with configurable timeouts (#12749)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR updates AscendStore's Yuanrong backend to use the synchronous
multi-buffer APIs introduced by openyuanrong-datasystem PR #1412:

- `mget_h2d_from_multi_buffers`
- `mset_d2h_from_multi_buffers`
- `batch_is_exist`

The connector already owns per-key device address and size arrays.
Passing those arrays directly avoids constructing per-blob Python/C++
wrapper objects and removes the legacy API-selection and compatibility
path.

It also consolidates Yuanrong client configuration in the JSON file
referenced by `YR_CONFIG_PATH`. In addition to the worker and Remote H2D
settings, users can configure:

| Option | Default | Purpose |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `connect_timeout_ms` | `9000` | Worker connection timeout |
| `request_timeout_ms` | `0` | Client request timeout; `0` keeps the SDK
fallback to the connection timeout |
| `get_sub_timeout_ms` | `0` | Object-ready wait passed to
`mget_h2d_from_multi_buffers` |

The obsolete `DS_WORKER_ADDR`, `DS_ENABLE_EXCLUSIVE_CONNECTION`, and
`DS_ENABLE_REMOTE_H2D` configuration path is removed. Related dead
helpers, redundant device checks, empty-key short-circuits, and per-key

`yuanrong.json` file. The backend now requires a Yuanrong Datasystem SDK
that provides the PR #1412 multi-buffer APIs.

Existing behavior is preserved by the documented defaults. The new
timeout fields are optional.

Example:

```json
{
    "worker_addr": "1.2.3.4:31501",
    "connect_timeout_ms": 9000,
    "request_timeout_ms": 0,
    "get_sub_timeout_ms": 0,
    "enable_remote_h2d": false,
```

[Feature][KV Pool] Support MTP and sparse C8 in layerwise prefill offload (#12853)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR extends the layerwise KV Pool to support MTP layers and sparse
C8 indexer caches in the prefill offload path.

Models using speculative decoding may introduce additional MTP layers
beyond the base transformer layers. Sparse attention models may also use
separated main KV and indexer cache groups, where a sparse C8 indexer
contains both data and scale tensors. The layerwise KV Pool must
understand these layouts to allocate, register, and transfer every cache
component using the correct physical layer mapping.

The main changes include:

- Extending the KV Pool physical layer layout to include MTP layers.
- Supporting separated SFA main and indexer cache groups.
- Supporting a variable number of cache tensors per physical layer.
- Adding per-layer cache offsets for correct address construction during
layerwise transfers.
- Allocating and registering sparse C8 indexer data and scale tensors.
- Updating transfer scheduling to use the effective layer count from the
complete cache layout.
- Updating logical KV cache memory accounting for MTP and sparse C8
layouts.
- Integrating these layouts with the physical buffer reuse mechanism
introduced in the previous PR.
- Validating supported multi-group layouts and preserving the original
behavior for incomplete layouts.

This PR covers MTP and sparse C8 support in the layerwise prefill
offload path. [RFC
#48203](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48203).

[BugFix] Restore synchronous AscendStore save (#13120)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Restore the `request_queue.join()` barrier in AscendStore
